entities.title: Should CI run the libraries' tests and the HASD validators?
entities.summary: CI checks the language-neutral material only; the five libraries' tests and the .dev validators run only where a contributor runs them.
entities.context: The libraries carry the obligations of implementations/README.md and must pass all everyday and text-form fixtures (docs/library-api.md §8), but validate.yml runs only tools/validate.py and tools/side_by_side.py --check. AGENTS.md asks every contributor to run each library's tests and, from now on, the two HASD validators before finishing; nothing checks that they did. Running five toolchains (.NET, Maven, Python, Node, Cargo) in CI costs build minutes and maintenance.

options.title: Keep CI as it is
options.consequences: Fast and cheap; a change that breaks a library or a .dev file is caught only by the next contributor who runs that check.

options.title: Add the HASD validators only
options.consequences: Two more Python steps with the jsonschema already installed; .dev files stay well-formed. Library behaviour stays unchecked.

options.title: Add one job per library, plus the validators
options.consequences: Every push proves every library against the shared fixtures; CI needs the five toolchains and takes longer.

blocks.description: Its notChecked entries for the library tests and the HASD validators stay until this is decided.
